moments.selftext: “A society that mocks virtue prepares its own collapse.” - Plato When a society begins to ridicule virtue, it gradually weakens the moral foundation it depends on to survive. In works such as The Republic, Plato emphasized qualities like justice, honesty, integrity, and self-discipline as essential principles that help create a stable and functioning society. These values are more than personal ideals; they help build the trust and responsibility necessary to hold a community together. When integrity is treated as weakness and good character becomes something to mock, people can become increasingly cynical and distrustful of one another. As mutual trust disappears, corruption and self-interest can begin to replace responsibility toward others. Over time, a society that consistently places individual desires above the common good may weaken from within, making its institutions and communities increasingly unstable.

At the same time, it's important to remember that OpenAI's DevDay is just around the corner, and as recently explained in the Axios article, Sam Altman stated that they will be releasing even more capable models very soon. GPT-Astra was just the beginning. And amidst all the excitement, we shouldn't forget that Grok 4.7 is also being released next week.
